steps: The Clever Courier Never Gets Hurt (Part I)
They say, ''If you're always by the river, your shoes are bound to get wet''... but this is a bit much, isn't it?
Early in the morning, I arrive at the forest on the outskirts of Port Bellin to collect the herbs that the client needs.
Sigh ... Hope I can find it soon.
The pay for gathering herbs isn't great, but for a Trekker like me who can't use magic, this kind of job is all I can really take on.
Not far ahead, you see strange patterns carved into the trunk of a large tree. Step closer for a better look—
Could it be claw marks left by an animal...? No, that's not it. They look more like human-made signs.
Bones… Could it be a warning about some kind of danger...?
Guess I'll try following the direction the fish head is pointing to. That patch of grass up ahead looks suspicious.
Whoa! A snare trap that yanks someone off the ground! Close call.
If it weren't for that sign, I would've walked right into it.
Whoever made that mark really did me a favor.
Oh no, someone else got trapped.
Cough, cough ... My throat's killing me ... ==B==And still no one's shown up.
Am I gonna be stuck here forever?
Could this be ... my life flashing before my eyes...? ==B==No! You are real! What are you doing here...?!
Just passing by. I'll get you out of here pronto. Worry about the rest later.
...Sooo, how did you end up falling into a trap like this?
I ... I accidentally stepped into a Shrubshrew hole...
Y-you saved me... Thank you, Boss～～～!!!
Trapped in this hole with no one coming to help ... I really thought I was going to starve out here… I'm so glad, meow～～～!!!
I noticed the trees around here all have fishbone marks showing where the traps are. You didn't see them?
Ah, so you noticed those marks. Yep, I drew them all, hehe.
There are groups of mischievous Shrubshrews roaming around in this forest. They are fighting over territory, so they've put a bunch of traps.
Teresa tosses a stone toward another spot marked with a fishbone. Many rotten tree fruits come crashing down from the trees.
Ugh...! It stinks...! If you fall into that trap, the smell probably won't come off for days...
But if you're sharp enough to spot traps that well hidden, how'd you end up falling into one of their holes?
Anyone walking by would be bound to notice a hole this size.
W-Wait! It's not like I fell in because I was dumb or anything! There was a reason!
This isn't a trap. This is a hole.
Uh ... ==B==I mean, you've made a good point.
I'm telling the truth! Look at these fish bone symbols.
The fish head shows the trap's direction, the number of bones tells you how many steps to take, and the size of the eye shows how dangerous it is.
See? I've had every detail covered, there's no way I'd fall for a trap!
Sure, the markings are really detailed, but they don't seem to have much to do with why you fell into the hole...
Never mind. Anyway, good job, Teresa!
Sounds like a back-handed compliment. But I'll take it, meow♪
I always leave a mark each time so that when others come into the forest, they won't fall into the traps.
That way, more people might venture out of the city. And more walkers mean more paths.
That's true ... I guess I've been saved by Teresa's markings myself. Thank you, Teresa. You really helped me out.
Wow...! You thanked me...! I think this the first time somebody did...?
Everyone else either say they can't tell the direction the fish heads are facing, or how many bones there are, or they don't even notice them at all...
Except for Donna and Freesia, people just say, "Trekkers can handle traps themselves, you're wasting your time"...
I don't see it that way. If people learn to read the markings, their trip would be a lot safer.
I think what you're doing is amazing, Teresa. Really, have more confidence in yourself.
Come think of it, what are you doing here, Boss?
Explore the Monolith like usual? There's no Monolith around here, I think.
I'm here for Purple Nettles. It's a herb that grows on steep hillsides and blooms with tiny purple flowers.
Oh yeah, Shrubshrews love munching on those. I know where they are. Follow me.
You really don't have to. What about your delivery run?
It's totally fine! You've helped me so much. Just think of it as my way to thank you!
Today's delivery destination is deep in this forest. We're headed the same way anyway.
Post Haste delivers to remote places like this?
Of course we do. In Donna's words: "A letter carries the writer's heart. No matter the distance, we must make sure they reach the other person."
So no matter if it's deep in the forest or underground, I'll make sure the letter gets delivered!
And if I mark the traps along the way, that could help others too, right?
If it means I can help others, a little extra work is totally worth it!
I remember they're in this direction. I'll go take a look.
Thanks. Watch out for the traps.
Don't worry, I've marked all the traps. I could dodge them with my eyes closed—==W==Whoa!
Why is there another Shrubshrew hole here?!
Please get me out of this hole, Boss ... Again.
Hmmm ... Is she really gonna be okay?
